items.prompt: Our new colleague ___ speak four languages, which is very useful.

explanation.en: Can + bare infinitive for general ability.

optionNotes.en: Can is a modal, so it needs no be.

items.prompt: Despite the storm, the pilot ___ land the plane safely.

explanation.en: One particular success in the past needs was able to; could is for general past ability.
explanation.es: Un logro concreto en pasado: was able to, no could.

optionNotes.en: Could does not describe a single successful event in an affirmative sentence.
Correct: was able to for one achievement in the past.
Can is present; the sentence is about the past.

items.prompt: Hi, it's me. ___ you pick up some milk on your way home?

explanation.en: Could you...? is a polite request.

optionNotes.en: Are you + infinitive does not make a request.
Do you pick up asks about a habit, not a favour.

items.prompt: Since the operation, she hasn't ___ run more than a mile.

explanation.en: The present perfect needs be able to, because can has no participle.
explanation.es: Can no tiene participio: «no ha podido» es hasn't been able to.

items.prompt: I hope that by next summer I'll ___ speak Italian without notes.

explanation.en: After will, can needs be able to.
explanation.es: Tras will, can no existe: will be able to.

optionNotes.en: Could does not fit this future meaning after I'll.
